character: Alliant's Couple and Family Therapy program is one program run in five places — San Diego, Irvine, Los Angeles, Sacramento and Online — and the 2025–26 program manual states flatly that all five "share the same curriculum, degree requirements, policies, and procedures." What the manual does not say, and what the COAMFTE-required disclosure data does, is how lopsided the five are. Entering MA cohorts on the ground run 13 to 43 students per campus per year; the online branch enrolled 111 to 190 per year over the same period. So the modal Alliant MFT student is an online student in a cohort roughly ten times the size of the Sacramento or Irvine class. The same disclosures show the tradeoff honestly: on-ground graduation-in-advertised-time rates run 55–95% depending on campus and year, the online rate runs 48–69%, while licensure rates sit at 87–100% across all of them.

The thing that most concretely distinguishes an Alliant trainee from a graduate of a BBS-only California program is COAMFTE accreditation, which the MA and PsyD hold and the PhD is still seeking. Because of it, the practicum requires 300 direct client contact hours of which at least 150 must be relational — couples or families, not individuals — plus 100 hours of supervision, at least 50 of it based on direct observation or audio/video recording. California's BBS imposes no relational-hours floor, so this shapes the caseload you have to negotiate for and the sites that will work. Alliant tells students to watch the ratio and keep relational-to-individual hours near 1:1. The systemic identity is not just accreditation paperwork, either: past CFT faculty included Jay Haley, James Framo, Virginia Satir, Carl Whitaker and Ivan Boszormenyi-Nagy, and Susan Johnson, who developed Emotionally Focused Therapy, is currently affiliated with the program. The curriculum reflects it — two semesters of systemic theory, each paired with a separate one-unit skills lab as a co-requisite (63120 with 63130, then 63220 with 63230), with the second semester moving into postmodernism and social constructionism plus "several empirically based models that private and public agencies are using across the state of California."

The criticism is real and worth stating with numbers rather than adjectives. Alliant converted from nonprofit to a for-profit benefit corporation in February 2015 under Arist Education System, a Bertelsmann subsidiary, and rebranded as "Alliant University" in January 2026. On-ground MA tuition is $1,463 per unit for 2026–27 and online is $1,135 — 60 units works out to roughly $87,800 on campus and $68,100 online, which is the reverse of USC, where both modalities cost the same. Federal College Scorecard data for Alliant–San Diego master's completers in the mental-health-services field show median federal graduate loan debt of $107,070 against median earnings of $53,383 one year after graduating. Student reviews are genuinely split, and the split is informative: the MFT-specific reviews on GradReports are positive ("the professors seem to care a lot... extremely culturally diverse and social justice oriented"), while the most damning reviews on that same page come from other Alliant programs — Clinical Counseling, School Psychology, Education — calling the school a "degree mill" with "minimal to nonexistent" instruction. If you are evaluating this program, do not average those together; they are describing different departments.
orientation: Systemic / relational couple and family therapy — explicitly model-based, taught as an integration of the major schools of family therapy

signature.title: MFT Techniques Lab I and II
signature.desc: Lab I: "An introduction to communication processes which are fundamental to interviewing and psychotherapy of couples and families. Includes skills such as empathy, listening, question-asking, probes, enactments, assessment of clients from an individual and systemic perspective and treatment planning..." Lab II: "An intensive lab focused on fundamental and advanced family therapy skills."
signature.why: These are co-requisites, not electives: you cannot take the theory course without simultaneously taking the lab that drills the corresponding skills. Splitting technique out into its own graded 1-unit lab twice in the first year is unusual — most California programs fold role-play into the theory course and hope it happens.

signature.title: Preparing for Community Practice
signature.desc: "A preparation and screening for community-based field training designed to facilitate integration of foundational conceptual, perceptual, executive, evaluative, and professional skills... This course utilizes clinical role-plays to assist in preparing for field training including systemic clinical assessment and collaborative, systemic treatment planning. Topics include public service delivery and support systems, case management, wraparound services, and interdisciplinary relations."
signature.why: Note the word "screening." This is an explicit gate — you must pass it before you may start practicum — and its content (wraparound services, case management, interdisciplinary relations) tells you the program expects most graduates to land in public and community mental health, not private practice.

signature.title: MFT Practicum
signature.desc: "The practicum program requires 300 hours of direct client contact, 150 of which must be with couples or families; students receive 100 hours of individual and group supervision, at least 50 hours of which are based on direct observation, videotape or audiotape. Students must be enrolled in a practicum course until all hour requirements are complete."
signature.why: The 150 relational hours and 50 hours of raw-data (recorded or live-observed) supervision are COAMFTE requirements that California's BBS does not impose. They make the degree portable to other states and they make your training more observable — but they also constrain which sites can host you, because the site has to be able to feed you couples and families and permit recording.

signature.title: MFT Theories and Techniques II
signature.desc: "This course covers philosophical concepts of postmodernism and social constructionism, examines the role of theory in philosophy, politics, epistemology, empirical investigation, and conceptual frameworks. In addition, the student will become very familiar with several empirically based models that private and public agencies are using across the state of California."
signature.why: The second half of that description is the practical one: this is where you learn the specific evidence-based models California county agencies actually contract for, which is the difference between being hireable at a community mental health agency and having to be trained from scratch.

signature.title: Diversity and the Family
signature.desc: "Examines diversity in the family including issues of ethnicity, race, religion, gender, gender-roles, sexual orientation, and social class. Blends systemic theory, research and practice, as students learn to work with diversity issues in families and with families having differing cultures, values, and needs."
signature.why: This is a practicum prerequisite, not a later elective — you cannot see clients until you have passed it, along with law and ethics, psychopathology, both theory courses and both labs. That sequencing is a deliberate statement about what the program considers foundational.

signature.title: Chemical Dependency and the Family
signature.desc: "Examines definitions of chemical dependency relative to the family. Discussion of etiology, medical aspects, evaluation of the family and treatment approaches, legal aspects, special populations, community resources and referral processes."
signature.why: This is the anchor of an embedded Chemical Dependency concentration that carries CAADE accreditation and adds no extra coursework or hours — you satisfy it by choosing a practicum site (residential or intensive outpatient) where at least 250 of your 300 required client hours involve addiction. A specialization paid for with placement choice rather than tuition is rare.

curriculum.note: Cohort model, six semesters over two full years (part-time plans run 3–4 years; the maximum time limit is 5 years). All campuses and the online branch follow the same Master Plan of Study. Fall and spring semesters are 15 weeks, summers 10 weeks. 57 core units plus one 3-unit elective; graduation also requires passing a comprehensive exam in May of the second year and logging 50 professional development hours, up to 25 of which may be personal therapy.

terms.label: Year 2 — Fall (9 units)
courses: PSY73300 Chemical Dependency and the Family (3)

practicum.starts: Three consecutive semesters, beginning either the first summer or the second fall depending on when you secure a site. You must pass PSY63100, 63110, 63120, 63130, 63220, 63230, 63260 and 63600 first — the program tells you to start the site search at least three months out and no later than the spring of your first year.
practicum.hours: 300 direct client contact hours, of which at least 150 must be relational (couples or families); 100 hours of supervision, at least 50 based on direct observation or recording. Benchmarks are 50 clinical hours in semester one, 125 in semester two, 125 in semester three. Separately, 50 professional development hours are required, up to 25 of which may be your own therapy with a fully licensed clinician who is not Alliant core faculty. Alliant estimates about 20 hours a week at the site, and says the practicum year can yield 600 to 1,300 hours toward the BBS 3,000.
practicum.clinic: None named in current materials. The 2025–26 program manual describes students "working in one of several community-based clinics with client families," but the clinical training manual is unambiguous that securing the site is the student's job; certain agencies near each campus have standing agreements with the university.
practicum.detail: The Clinical Training Manual states it plainly: "As a student of the CFT program, you are fully responsible in securing your practicum site." Each campus has a Clinical Training Coordinator who approves sites and hours, and there is an approved-site list plus a Practicum Site Qualification Checklist, but you interview and get hired. Final approval requires malpractice insurance, current AAMFT membership, a signed agency agreement from all parties, and a signed acknowledgement of the manual — missing any one gets you dropped from PSY73600. Supervision is doubled up: weekly face-to-face (Zoom for online students) with an Alliant faculty member in the practicum class, plus weekly supervision from your on-site supervisor. A critical constraint for online students: "You must obtain a site in the State in which you reside, even if that site is telehealth. Your site and your clients must be located in your State of current residence."
practicum.model_evidence: As a student of the CFT program, you are fully responsible in securing your practicum site.

admissions.cohort_size: From COAMFTE-required disclosures, entering MA cohorts: San Diego 29–43, Irvine 14–19, Los Angeles 11–20, Sacramento 13–21, Online 111–190 per year (2020–21 through 2025–26).
admissions.prereqs: General graduate admission: bachelor's from a regionally accredited institution, minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA unless the program states otherwise, two letters of recommendation, a 2–4 page essay, a CV, and an admissions interview where the program requires one. Alliant does not publish MFT-specific prerequisite coursework.
admissions.deadline: Rolling — the MA runs on both a semester calendar (fall/spring/summer starts) and an eight-week term calendar, and is "open for enrollment during each of those respective enrollment periods." No fixed application deadline is published.
admissions.gre_evidence: minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale unless otherwise stated

Alliant's current 2025–26 catalog is behind an AWS bot challenge — preview_program.php and content.php both return an empty challenge page. Course descriptions quoted here come from Alliant's own archived 2022–23 catalog entries, which are still served. Two courses in the current plan of study have changed since then: PSY63173 Parent-Child Therapy is now 3 units (was PSY63170, 2 units) and PSY67562 Psychopharmacology is now 2 units (was PSY67560, 3 units). No current description could be retrieved for either.

Irvine is listed on the COAMFTE disclosure pages and in the program manual, but the MA program page's 'Program Offered In' box lists only Los Angeles, Sacramento, San Diego and Online. Could not resolve whether Irvine is still taking new MA students; the Irvine cohort data shows 15 entering in 2024–25 and 19 in 2025–26.
The PhD in MFT is described in the 2025–26 manual as "currently in the process of seeking COAMFTE accreditation." The MA and PsyD are accredited.
No in-house training clinic could be confirmed. The program manual and an older catalog both reference community-based clinics, but no named Alliant-operated MFT clinic exists in current materials.
No MFT-specific GRE policy, GPA cutoff, admit rate or prerequisite coursework list is published; only Alliant's general graduate requirements.

College Scorecard reports at the 4-digit CIP level (51.15) and by campus, so the $107,070 median debt figure covers Alliant–San Diego master's completers across mental-health-services programs, not the MFT MA alone.

outcomes.as_published: Licensure rate is the percentage of graduates from the cohort year that have achieved ANY level of MFT licensure. ... Alliant MFT Notes: Licensure rates include any graduate who achieves ANY level of postgraduate MFT licensure (e.g. associate, provisional, or registered, as applicable per jurisdiction).
outcomes.school_note: FIVE SEPARATE TABLES, one per campus/modality (Irvine, San Diego, Los Angeles, Sacramento, Online) - each its own PDF; there is no combined Alliant figure and none should be constructed. A 'campus' key has been added to each cohort row to keep them distinguishable. Alliant is the ONLY school in this set that spells out in its own added note that 'licensure' counts associate/provisional/registered status - i.e. these are NOT independently licensed LMFTs. Graduation rates are markedly lower than the CA average here (many in the 44-69% range) because the advertised length is 2 years; students finishing later are counted as non-completers. Cohort sizes vary enormously WITHIN the same institution (n=11 at Sacramento vs n=190 online), so per-campus rates are not equally reliable. Sacramento 2017-2018 licensure of 63% falls below COAMFTE's own 70% benchmark. Individual campus PDFs: files.alliant.edu/institutional-information/accreditations/clinical-psychology/coamfte-student-achievement-data-ma-{irvine,san-diego,los-angeles,sacramento,online}.pdf
